energy-us-1980-1990.title: Main sources of energy in the USA (1980 & 1990)
energy-us-1980-1990.prompt:
The given graph shows the main sources of energy for USA in 1980 and 1990.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
energy-us-1980-1990.overview: Oil remained the largest energy source in both years, although its share fell. Coal and nuclear power increased, while natural gas decreased slightly and hydroelectric power was unchanged.
guide: Compare the relative importance of the five energy sources in 1980 and 1990.
Oil and natural gas: describe their initial dominance and changes over time.
Coal, nuclear power and hydroelectric power: compare increases and stability.

water-use-regions.title: Water usage in San Diego, California and worldwide
water-use-regions.prompt:
The pie charts below compare water usage in San Diego, California and the rest of the world.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
water-use-regions.overview: Domestic consumption made up the highest share in San Diego County and California, whereas agriculture dominated worldwide. Industrial water use represented 23% both in San Diego and globally.
guide: Compare the main use of water in each location.
Group San Diego and California because residential use is highest in both.
Contrast worldwide agricultural dominance with the residential patterns in the two US locations.

social-media-age-groups.title: Age distribution of users on Facebook, YouTube and Twitter
social-media-age-groups.prompt:
The pie charts show the proportion of users across different age groups on three apps: Twitter, Facebook and YouTube.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
social-media-age-groups.overview: Adults aged 18–49 made up the largest combined proportion of users across all three platforms. Twitter was particularly popular with the 18–34 age group, while older adults formed smaller shares everywhere.
guide: Identify the largest and smallest age segments on each platform.
Compare Facebook and YouTube, which have relatively similar age profiles.
Discuss Twitter's comparatively high percentage of 18–34-year-olds and the smaller shares of the youngest and oldest users.
